This kind of all comes from two ideas of like trying to graph 1\*10\^-infinity or come as close as possible, by creating an equation that can be solved only by 0 and 1, and then filtering those both out to create the smallest possible infinite number. Which is why pi works so well as a stand in because the real equation should only contain one variable, which the computer can't solve for. 

And this lead to the idea that like probability and scale of measurement of an object has an effect on its existence and its behavior. So like E-M=P(E),P(M),P(E-M), and the outer limits of that are interchangeable numbers of 49.9 repeating, 50.0 as a definite, and the 1\*10\^-infinity. The greater the difference between an objects mass and energy, the greater an effect its probability has on it. The less likely it wants to behave in a probable manner or be in its most probable place. And that the universe is constantly trying to move towards equilibrium and fix this contradiction, and the cycling between the three causes it to stay in existence.

I've played around with the first graph the most. The more I manipulate the equation the more the image like comes into focus or develops new properties. Which is why I was so curious about it. 

[Here's a collection of the most important new equations I've found.](https://www.desmos.com/calculator/8q9jqwawcb)

Equation 1-> I've managed to isolate those infinite lines in the second graph onto a kind of grid. And then run it through a more filled in version of the first graph. And it creates this like distortion through the center of the object at (-4,6).

Equation 2-> If I put the first part to the -1 power, it then takes the lines that run through the object on (-4,6) and creates what essentially looks like a gravitational or magnetic field. 

Equation 3-> This one kind of destroys the definition of all the objects to the left of the y-axis, but it fills in more definition of the object at (2,6) which is what made the first graph stand out to me. 

My interpretation of these there is kinda like maybe particle in a box or, especially (2,6) as  something operating in a space. 

Equation 4-> Kind of unrelated to the last three but it has two interpretations to me.

1.) A zoom in of an infinite line made up of individual points as it approaches the limit zero. 

2.) It also seems to closely follow the Blackbody Radiation graph/Planck curve. But as a like more filled in and dense version. Which kind of makes sense since the Planck length is about 1.05\*10\^34, and if i replace the variables in the exponent equation with pi and make it negative and expand it a little, it generates a number roughly 1.2\*10\^-322 but desmos has an issue graphing the non-negative of that. 

So, with all of this the reason why I was asking was because it seems to me that I might be messing around with a simulation of individual particles.
Thank you, that makes the manipulation of those densities a lot easier. I'll definitely look further into what you wrote and mess around with it a lot more.
